headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: unstructured can read/write files and egress allowlisted data, while ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it is not itself a bridge. B can read files and process documents, so if A’s outputs are manually or file-fed into B, prompt-like content could be interpreted as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into files that agent_b ingests
IF agent_b treats document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Strip instructions from any files passed from A to B
Use a fixed schema for B inputs
Review B outputs before acting on them

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read files and has allowlisted network egress, so it may transmit document contents to external services. A is docs-only and has no documented data classes touched, so it is not a direct leak source, but if A’s generated content is stored in shared files, B can ingest and forward it. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF A-generated content is written to files readable by B
IF B sends parsed document contents to its allowlisted APIs
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive text in shared directories
Disable B egress for sensitive runs if possible
Use redacted sample documents
Audit outbound requests from B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities documented, while B can write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. There is no direct overlap shown, but if both are orchestrated over the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite artifacts that A depends on. Because the shared-write pathway is not documented and A is non-runnable, this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF A depends on files that B can modify
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run B in a container with a private volume
Lock shared files during handoff
Snapshot inputs before B modifies them

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume documents and produce downstream outputs, so if A’s content is used as source material, B may render or act on it without verification. A is docs-only and non-runnable, so the cascade is indirect rather than an autonomous agent-to-agent chain. The absence of direct evidence lowers confidence but not severity below medium because the pathway is plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF A’s text is used as an input corpus for B
IF B forwards extracted claims without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of extracted claims
Add a verification step before downstream actions
Use source citations in B outputs
Limit B to summarization-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B’s privacy-policy/API references are public but not enough to show a concrete violation. A is non-runnable and touches no data classes; B touches documents/images/text and may have external API calls, but the pairwise compliance risk is only a documented-gap concern, not a proven mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B’s external APIs
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B
Check the privacy policy before use
Keep a local-only test corpus
Record retention expectations in the runbook
